❯ Write 300 words about rivers. No tools.

⏺ Rivers are among the oldest sculptors on Earth. Given enough time, a modest stream can carve a canyon, and the Colorado has cut through rock for millions of years to expose layers of geological
  history in the walls of the Grand Canyon. Rivers shape the land as they flow, eroding banks, depositing sediment, and slowly shifting their courses across broad floodplains.

  Every river begins somewhere. Some rise from snowmelt in high mountains, others from springs that seep out of underground aquifers, and others from the rain that gathers across a wide basin. Each
  one collects water from a network of smaller tributaries, and that network is called a drainage basin. Everything that falls within the basin's edges eventually finds its way toward the same outlet,
  whether that is a lake, a sea, or a desert where the water simply evaporates.

  Rivers have always mattered to people. Early civilizations rose along the Nile, the Tigris and Euphrates, the Indus, and the Yellow River, because flooding deposited fertile soil and the water could
  be channeled to grow crops. Cities grew at river crossings and river mouths, where trade routes met. Even today, many of the world's largest urban areas sit on riverbanks, relying on them for
  drinking water, transport, power, and industry.

  Rivers also support enormous amounts of life. Fish migrate upstream to spawn, birds nest in riverside forests, and insects, amphibians, and mammals depend on the constant flow and the nutrients it
  carries. Healthy rivers filter pollutants, store floodwater, and recharge groundwater, but they are fragile. Dams, pollution, drought, and climate change can disrupt their rhythms and harm the
  ecosystems that depend on them.

  Rivers remind us that the landscape is never fixed. Their paths bend, split, and sometimes abandon old channels altogether. A river is never quite the same from one season to the next, yet it
  remains recognizably itself, carrying the story of the land it crosses toward the sea.
